_comment: Where the four-view turnaround lives on each production reference sheet. Read by tools/art_pipeline/crop_views.py.
_comment_band: `band` is [x0, y0, x1, y1] in source pixels: a rectangle containing the turnaround row and NOTHING else — no view labels, no head close-up, no swatch strip, no detail panels. Read off a coordinate-grid overlay; regenerate one with `crop_views.py --grid` if a sheet is ever redrawn.
_comment_centres: `centres` are approximate x positions of the four figures within the band, in source pixels, left to right. Approximate is enough: the script snaps each to the tight bounding box of whatever content sits around it, so being 20px out costs nothing and being 200px out fails loudly.
_comment_why_not_automatic: An earlier version segmented the four figures automatically from a column-density profile. It worked, but only inside a narrow window of three threshold values across the four sheets — the drop shadows pool at the figures' feet and bridge the gaps, so the parameters that split Terrapup's legs from its neighbour also split Galewisp's wing from its body. Four numbers per sheet, read once off a grid and committed, are more robust than a heuristic tuned to the edge of failure.
_comment_layout: The four sheets do not share a layout. Sheet 01 puts its FRONT/SIDE/BACK/3-4 labels BELOW the figures and 02 puts them ABOVE, so one hard-coded band would swallow text on one sheet and clip ears on another.
_comment_scale: All four views on a sheet are drawn at one scale, and the crops preserve it: every view of a species is cut at the same square size and emitted at the same resolution, differing only in horizontal centre. Multi-image-to-3D uses apparent scale to reconcile views, so normalising each view to its own bounding box would tell the generator the creature changes size when it turns around.
_comment_output: 1024 square. Source figures are 180-450px wide, so this upscales 2-5x. Deliberate: generators downweight or reject small inputs, and a clean upscale of flat stylised art costs nothing. The real fidelity ceiling is the sheet and no resampling moves it.

terrapup._comment: Labels sit below the feet at y~447, so the band stops at 415. Starts at x=20 to clear the sheet's own black outer frame, which is not background and would otherwise be cropped in beside the front view.

ripplet._comment: Labels are ABOVE this row at y~137, so the band starts at 155. The side and 3/4 tail fins are the widest thing here and must not be clipped — they are a defining feature.

galewisp._comment: Ear tufts reach y~110 and the spread wings make this the widest turnaround of the four. Labels below at y~463.

trainer._comment: A standing human, so each figure is much taller than it is wide. Labels below at y~565. Starts at x=60 to clear the TETHERBOUND wordmark. `extra_boxes` adds the sheet's own head close-up at native scale, because the face is ~150px in a full-body crop and every round-1 and round-2 candidate came back with no eye sockets at all.

warden._comment: THREE views, not four: board 06 gives the Warden front/side/back plus a head close-up, and a bust at a different scale is not a fourth turnaround view. The owner approved this board as the Warden's source (docs/art/REFERENCE_CANON.md), replacing board 07's off-brief priestess.

grandpa._comment: EXPLICIT boxes, measured, after the blind critique traced a floating dagger in one candidate and a shredded ghost figure in another back to MY crops: every view carried a sliver of the neighbouring board figure at its left edge, and the generator dutifully modelled it. The staff-holding fourth figure is dropped entirely rather than cropped around, since a staff fused to the arm is exactly what the build prompt forbids. `head` is the board's own portrait at native scale — at full-body 1024 the face is ~150px and the eyes are ~10, which is why all six humanoid candidates came back with no eyes at all.

sheets._comment_npc_bases: `docs/art/reference/12_NPC_Bases_Reusable.png`, made canon by D24/NP1. THREE rows, one base body per row, each with FIVE turnaround views (FRONT, 3/4 FRONT, SIDE, 3/4 BACK, BACK) at one shared scale per row -- more than any other sheet in the pack. `crop_sheet()` requires `len(centres) == len(views)` and `figure_bounds()` places a divider between every ADJACENT pair of declared centres, so a column cannot simply be dropped from `centres` without also dropping it from `views` -- doing that would put the SIDE/BACK divider in the middle of the skipped 3/4-BACK figure instead of the gap that is actually there, corrupting both neighbours. So all five columns are named and cropped, and the one this pipeline has no use for is given a throwaway name (`_unused_three_quarter_back`) rather than one `meshy.py`'s VIEWS list recognises -- `reference_views()` only looks for front/side/back/three_quarter/head, so the extra file sits in the directory and is never read. `three_quarter` is bound to the 3/4 FRONT column rather than 3/4 BACK because it shows the face.

villager_female._comment: Row 1, FEMALE VILLAGER BASE. See _comment_npc_bases for why all five columns are named. `mask` paints out a small decorative flourish beside the row's own title ('1. FEMALE VILLAGER BASE'), which sits inside the band just left of the FRONT figure's hair and rode into the first crop as a floating grey sliver until this was added — the same failure the Grandpa and wild-sheet masks exist to prevent.

villager_male._comment: Row 2, MALE VILLAGER BASE. Same column layout and same reasoning as villager_female, one row down. No stray title flourish on this row's heading, so no mask.

grunt._comment: Row 3, TEAM TETHER GRUNT BASE. Same column layout and same reasoning as villager_female. Band starts at 662, not 655 like the other two rows would suggest, because the panel rule between rows 2 and 3 sits at y=655-658 here (rows 1 and 2's own dividers sit above their bands and are already excluded). This row's boots also sit close enough to its own FRONT/3-4 FRONT/SIDE/3-4 BACK/BACK caption row that there is no clean gap between feet-shadow and label ink to cut the band on, unlike rows 1 and 2 — `mask` blanks the caption instead so content_rows() finds the true foot-bottom on its own.

sheets._comment_wild: THE MEADOWS WILD ROSTER, from the owner's canon pack (docs/art/reference/wild/). Their sheets are laid out differently from 01-04: each species gets a hero illustration, a THREE-view turnaround (front/side/back — there is no drawn 3/4 view), a head close-up, action poses, a palette strip and a scale figure, and three or four species share one 1448px sheet. So each entry takes the turnaround as its band — three views at one shared scale, which is the signal multi-view reconstruction needs — and adds the HERO as `three_quarter` through extra_boxes, at its own scale. The hero is worth the scale break: a turnaround figure here is 80-170 source pixels wide against 180-450 on sheets 01-04, and the hero is two to three times that. `mask` paints out the species name and role line, which sit inside the hero's own panel with no rectangle that holds the figure and excludes the words.
sheets._comment_wild_sheet05: 05_Meadows_Wild_Scale_Palette_Implementation_Guide.png IS MISNAMED. It is Ground Sheet B — Meadowhart, Burrowback and Tuskroot — not a scale guide. The file name is the owner's and is left alone; this comment is the correction.

trailpup._comment: The band starts at 758 because this row's FRONT/SIDE/BACK labels run to y=755, measured — three pixels of 'BACK' survived a band starting at 752 and rode into every crop.

galecrest._comment: TWO turnaround views, not three. The sheet prints FRONT and SIDE over a SINGLE wide spread-wing profile figure — there is no separate front view drawn. Declaring three centres here would split that one hawk down the middle and hand the generator two half-birds.

veridian._comment: EXPLICIT BOXES, not band+centres. Four stags are drawn on this panel at two different scales, two of them overlap antler-to-antler, and an inset eye-detail panel sits under the middle pair — no trough divider can separate that, and the auto-split duly returned one crop containing three animals. Two hand-read boxes around the two hero views are the honest answer; the escape hatch exists for exactly this.

sheets._comment_expansion: THE MEADOWS CREATURE EXPANSION, from docs/owner-direction/TETHERBOUND_MEADOWS_CREATURE_EXPANSION.md and its ten boards (docs/art/reference/creature-expansion-2026-08-30/). Five of the nine named creatures are NEW MESHY builds with no existing mesh (Sparkit, Cindercub, Shadelet, Bramblebun-redesign, Frostclaw); the other four are recolor/VFX jobs on existing meshes and need no crops here. All five entries below share ONE source file, the 1536x1024 master sheet, which draws all nine creatures on a 3x3 grid of identical per-species panels: title/type/build-path/role, a HERO illustration, a FRONT/SIDE/BACK turnaround, a TOP/BOTTOM pair, a palette strip and build notes. TWO DECISIONS were made reading this sheet, not assumed: (1) NO three_quarter view. Per-creature sheets 03-09 (the individual boards, not this master) draw a HERO pose that is roughly 3/4, and the obvious move is to feed it as a fourth view the way the wild sheets' extra_boxes do for their own hero panels. Checked against this sheet's actual poses and rejected: the master's own hero panel (and every per-creature sheet's hero) is a crouched or prowling ACTION pose -- weight low, one or more paws planted forward -- while the front/side/back turnaround is uniformly a neutral standing pose. The wild-sheet precedent this mirrors got away with a scale break because the pose was still neutral; here the pose itself differs, and multi-image-to-3D reconciles what a subject IS across images, not just its size -- a fourth image fighting the other three on POSE is a worse defect than the one omitting it avoids. Front/side/back only. Full reasoning and the crouch/prowl evidence are in ralph/reports/handover-T1-CREATURE-MESH-2026-08-30.md. (2) TOP is real and new. Unlike every prior sheet in this pack, these boards draw a genuine orthographic top-down view per creature, at a scale the tool can reconcile with the turnaround well enough to be worth sending -- and `meshy.py`'s VIEWS already lists 'top' (added for props, never used by a creature until now), so no code change was needed to make it count as a real fourth input. Cut via `extra_boxes` at the TOP box's own scale, same mechanism the wild sheets use for their hero panel, since the top view sits in its own sub-panel below the turnaround rather than sharing its band. FIDELITY: every front/side/back figure on this sheet measures roughly 80-190 source px per side -- below this pipeline's established 180-450px range, and for Bramblebun specifically (the one creature where quality matters most, being common) a real concern rather than a formality. Recorded in the handover rather than silently accepted. THIN CELL-DIVIDER RULES: every panel on this sheet draws a hairline box border around each FRONT/SIDE/BACK cell, at a contrast this sheet's own `erase_dividers()` does not treat as faint (its DIVIDER_MAX_DISTANCE=105 assumes the pale rules on sheets 01-04; these read past that), so each entry below carries an explicit `mask` for the ones that fall inside its own band and would otherwise crop in as a line through the creature's own body -- found the hard way, via a first --check contact sheet.

sparkit._comment: Panel 3 of 9, row 1 col 3. Band excludes a stray flourish from the BUILD PATH badge/hero-image smoke that reaches to x=1218 at this row's height -- there is a clean zero-ink gap at x=1220-1230 the band starts just past. No cell-divider mask needed here: this row's rules happen to fall inside the natural figure gaps. TOP box is the flattened top-down figure, own scale via extra_boxes, cut clear of the hero image (which reaches to ~x=1218 at this y too) and the BOTTOM box (starts ~x=1390).

cindercub._comment: Panel 4 of 9, row 2 col 1. Same per-row template as Sparkit, one row down (row 2's label sits at y~367-373 vs row 1's y~20-25, content band is the same ~115-120px tall). Band starts at x=270 to clear the hero image's own flame/smoke, confirmed by eye to be hero bleed and not the front figure's own tail-flame. `mask` paints out the front/side cell's own divider rule at x=346: left alone, the first --check contact sheet showed it as a hairline cutting through Cindercub's own body, with a sliver of the neighbouring figure bleeding through where the line had widened the front figure's own snapped edge -- the same failure Grandpa's mask entry describes.

shadelet._comment: Panel 5 of 9, row 2 col 2. EXPLICIT BOXES, not band+centres -- see the correction below for why. `mask`'s first rectangle clears the front/side cell-divider rule that falls inside the front box; the second clears the band's own right edge inside the back box. Its former third rectangle (934-939, the side/back divider) is gone: that column no longer falls inside any declared box, so masking it is unnecessary rather than newly harmless. TRADE-OFF, accepted deliberately: FRONT's own tail curl and SIDE's own head sit close enough in x (front's tail dips down to about x=884 at the same x-range where side's snout starts at x=846) that no single rectangle can hold all of front's tail without also reaching into side's head. front's box stops at x=846, clipping roughly the outer half of its tail curl, rather than risk bleeding side's head into front's crop -- the worse failure by this pipeline's own precedent (Grandpa's floating dagger). This does not lose the signature 'long curling tail' feature from the reference set overall: BACK's own box captures a full, complete, uncropped spiral, and TOP shows the tail's full length again from above -- front alone doesn't need to carry it. CORRECTION, found on user review, in two stages. STAGE 1 (wrong): an earlier version of this comment claimed Shadelet's side view is drawn with a visible gap in its tail coil and called that the source art, not a crop defect. Wrong -- the sheet draws a small unrelated decorative spiral flourish in the gap between the SIDE and BACK cells, and it was riding into side.png because the old band+centres setup shares ONE top/bottom across all three views (content_rows()), and BACK's own tail legitimately reaches y~498, which dragged SIDE's crop down far enough to sweep up the unrelated spiral sitting below SIDE's own real content (which itself ends at y~451, confirmed by connected-component analysis). STAGE 2 (also wrong): the first fix tried a `mask` rectangle over the spiral instead, on the theory that its only contact with real content was a thin antialiasing bridge into BACK's tail around x=948-955. Rendering it out proved that wrong too -- the fill this pipeline's own MASK_RING samples averaged in enough of BACK's own dark ink from that near-touching edge to paint a solid dark rectangle into back.png, a worse defect than the one being fixed. EXPLICIT BOXES are the actual fix: SIDE's own box stops at y=455, well above the spiral, and BACK's box starts at x=950, well clear of the spiral's own right edge -- neither box's rectangle intersects the spiral's pixels at all, so no masking of it is needed or present. Confirmed by inspecting the rendered front/side/back/top crops after this fix, not assumed from the source alone.

bramblebun_redesign._comment: Panel 6 of 9, row 2 col 3. NOT keyed as `bramblebun` -- an existing `assets/creatures/tetherbound/bramblebun/reference/` from the old design stays in place until the new build is judged better (owner brief, and CLAUDE.md's own 'preserve working behaviour outside scope'). This is a REPLACEMENT candidate, not an edit of the original entry, so it gets its own key and its own output directory. This panel's own label sits unusually close to its content -- only ~5px of clearance before the ear tips start, tighter than the other four panels -- so a first band starting lower to protect the label instead swallowed the ear tips, and a first band starting at y=372 to protect the ears instead baked the FRONT/SIDE/BACK text into the top of all three crops (seen on a first --check contact sheet). Fixed by masking the label row instead of moving the band off it, so the tight ear-tip clearance is kept. `mask` also covers the front/side cell divider at x=1322 and the band's own left edge, the same rule-line defect as Cindercub and Shadelet. The TOP box's creature overflows the sheet's own drawn box (antler branches reach above it, root/leg tendrils reach below) -- read off a wider crop of the source rather than trusted to the box outline.

frostclaw._comment: Panel 9 of 9, row 3 col 3. Shortest turnaround band of the five (~95px vs ~115-125px for the others) -- Frostclaw's standing cat pose is simply less vertical than the others' raised ears/antlers, confirmed by eye, not a misread band. `mask` paints out this row's front/side and side/back cell-divider rules, same defect and fix as the other four. First TOP-box estimate was read off the sheet's own box outline width and came back with the tail clipped on a --check pass; the actual painted creature runs wider than its box on this row too, so the fixed box was read off a wider source crop instead.
